react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment group's metabolome is defined by a robust, cross-paradigm signal in eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167 Eicosanoid synthesis). Five lipid mediators derived from arachidonic acid were simultaneously elevated: arachidonic acid itself (KEGG:C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5(S)-HETE (C04805), 15(S)-HETE (C04742), and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717). RaMP ORA ranked this pathway first among 15 returned (FDR=9.7e-14, fold enrichment 1430×), Mummichog ranked the corresponding KEGG arachidonic acid metabolism module first (p=8.4e-4, 13/13 input compounds mapped), and MetaboAnalystR listed KEGG:hsa00590 as the top hit. These three independent paradigms converge on the same biological module. Arachidonic acid is the canonical upstream substrate; the 5- and 15-HETE products reflect differential lipoxygenase (ALOX5/ALOX15) activity, while leukotriene A4 and 15-deoxy-PGJ2 signal engagement of the 5-lipoxygenase branch and the cyclooxygenase-derived cyclopentenone branch, respectively. Glycerol (C00116) participates in glycerophospholipid metabolism (Mummichog rank 2), consistent with membrane remodeling that accompanies eicosanoid biosynthesis. 2-Ketobutyric acid (C00109) maps to valine/leucine/isoleucine biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00290, p=0.035) and propanoate metabolism (KEGG:hsa00640), suggesting a secondary perturbation of branched-chain amino acid catabolism. 4-Hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156) and N-acetylgalactosamine (KEGG input C01074) did not reach significance in any single tool but N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (the structurally resolved analogue of N-acetylgalactosamine) appeared in sialic acid metabolism (Mummichog rank 5) and hyaluronan/N-glycan degradation (Mummichog ranks 7/13), indicating minor glycosylation-related changes. The convergent eicosanoid signal is the dominant biological story.

Mummichog m/z-direct analysis identified Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top-ranked module (p=0.000756), with all thirteen input metabolites mapped to that pathway. Both methods confirmed arachidonic acid as the primary substrate feeding the COX and lipoxygenase branches that generate the observed eicosanoids. The lipid arm—encompassing 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2—reflects engagement of the 5-lipoxygenase and cyclooxygenase pathways in parallel. Glycerol appeared in the mummichog network as a component of glycerophospholipid metabolism, consistent with broader lipid flux remodeling. The four peripheral compounds (N-acetylgalactosamine, 2-ketobutyric acid, 4-hydroxybenzoic acid) were not captured by the primary eicosanoid module in either paradigm.
